annotations.title: Investment lineup: every fund on the plan's Schedule of Assets, with ticker, name and dollars

description:
Every holding on the plan's Schedule of Assets (the list of investments attached to the Form 5500 as a
PDF), largest first: each fund's ticker and name, share class, fund family, vehicle type (mutual fund,
collective trust, separate account...), year-end dollars and share of the holdings. `fields` asks for
tickers only or names only.

Fund names and tickers are matched to the SEC's fund list, each with a `certainty`: sure, less sure or much
less sure (check before relying on it). Collective trusts and other non-registered holdings have no ticker
(`why_no_ticker` says why). A pooled separate account shows the fund it invests in, with `held_through`.
`check` says how the reading tied to Schedule H and the schedule's printed total; `asset_mix` gives the
Schedule H totals for context.

Lineups so far cover about 1,040 large plans (plan year 2024), chiefly plans with $1 billion or more. Other
plans answer `lineup_not_available`, which isn't charged. Nor is a lineup whose `check.status` is review (the
automatic checks didn't fully confirm it), or a master trust plan's, which lists only the master trust
interest. For fees use `get_plan_fees`.

Price: $0.25 per call, paid in USDC on Base (mainnet) with x402 (MCP transport), or from card credits (an app signed in at /connect, or an 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' header). Without payment the tool returns the payment requirements. Errors and empty results aren't charged.

Same data as GET /lineup of the Plan Data API.

fields.description: What each fund carries: both (the default) = ticker and name; ticker = tickers only (the name fields are null); name = names only (the ticker is null).
fields.title: Fields

plan_year.description: Plan year of the lineup. Default: the latest year with one.
plan_year.title: Plan Year

pn.description: Plan number (1-999). Optional when the EIN has one plan.
pn.title: Pn
